title: Recording: She’s My Baby, The Note You Never Wrote, Time To Hide by Wings | 1976
content:
Studio Two, Abbey Road Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Peter Henderson

Wings recorded overdubs for three Wings At The Speed Of Sound songs on 31 January 1976.

Paul and Linda McCartney and Denny Laine began by adding harmony vocals to ‘She’s My Baby’.

The McCartneys then recorded overdubs and an introduction for ‘The Note You Never Wrote’, using a Mellotron and Moog synthesizer. Six tracks of the multitrack tape were filled with sound effects, which appeared throughout the song.

The final day’s work was on ‘Time To Hide’. Denny Laine added a harmonica part and Paul McCartney and Jimmy McCulloch both performed lead guitar solos. The first half of the solo was played by McCartney using a Gizmotron, and McCulloch’s latter half was on a Fender Stratocaster with no additional gadgetry.

The Gizmotron was a device invented by 10cc’s Kevin Godley and Lol Creme, which attached to a guitar and bowed the strings to simulate the sound of orchestral string instruments. McCartney had previously used it on ‘Spirits Of Ancient Egypt’

Half of the thing was harmonica – it was a little chance because I used to play a lot of harmonica with The Moody Blues – and the other half was Paul playing guitar with Gizmo, which gave it a really different sound.
Denny Laine, 2014
Wings At The Speed Of Sound deluxe edition liner notes

After the session, McCartney met Fiachra Trench at 7 Cavendish Avenue. Trench had been commissioned to write orchestral arrangements for ‘The Note You Never Wrote’ and ‘Warm And Beautiful’. McCartney gave him a rough mix of the former, and a demo of the still-unrecorded latter song. The orchestral overdub session took place on 13 February.
